title: Senator Tan Parker discusses voting deadlines, October 7 anniversary, and Texas Cyber Command - Mid City Times
text:
Senator Tan Parker, who has represented Texas’s 12th Senate district since 2023, recently used his social media platform to address a range of legislative and public policy topics, including election registration deadlines, remembrance of international tragedies, and advancements in state cybersecurity.
On October 6, 2025, Parker reminded constituents of an important civic deadline, posting, “Today is the final day to register to vote in the November 4, 2025 election! On the ballot will be Constitutional Amendments proposed by the Texas Legislature — covering key issues like government operations, taxes, property rights, and more. If approved, these amendments become https://t.co/KLZtCPr2Qb”.
The following day, October 7, 2025, Parker marked the second anniversary of the October 7 attacks in Israel, stating, “Two years ago today, Hamas terrorists unleashed unimaginable horror—murdering over 1,200 innocent people and taking 251 hostages. As we remember the victims of #October7, we continue to pray for the return of every hostage and for justice to prevail. https://t.co/nx0vQYZMcj”.
Parker also highlighted Texas’s efforts in digital security on October 8, 2025, posting, “Texas is leading the nation in cybersecurity with the creation of the Texas Cyber Command! It’s a major step forward to protect 31 million Texans from digital threats. I’m was honored to spearhead the work to author and lead this effort to strengthen our defenses and keep Texas https://t.co/R8ccI8zxjL”.
Parker, a Republican, succeeded Angela Paxton in the Texas State Senate and has since been active in legislative initiatives related to state governance and security. The Texas Cyber Command was established as part of ongoing efforts to bolster the state’s digital infrastructure and safeguard its residents against evolving cyber threats.
